A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application of adrenalin locally in the course of LAVH and VH is an effective and safe haemostatic measure.
terlipressin is a safe alternative for the application of adrenalin in LAVH or vaginal hysterectomy.
the application of adrenalin in the vaginal part after LAVH and VH is superior to terlipressin, but it is associated with a higher incidence of hypertensive reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adrenalin should still be considered the first choice for local application in vaginal surgery.
adrenalin is still the best local haemostatic for the vaginal part of LAVG or VH, but its use should be limited to this specific area and not to the laparoscopic one.
